abstract: Máčajová, Mazzuoccolo and Tabarelli showed that if a minimum counterexample to the Berge–Fulkerson conjecture is cyclically 5-edge-connected but not cyclically 6-edge-connected, then the admissible sets of Berge–Fulkerson boundary types of the two 5-poles at any cycle-separating 5-edge-cut form one of 13 explicit pairs, Cases I–XIII. We prove that nine of these cases are impossible: no cubic 5-pole of any order has admissible set equal to the set $L^*$ of Cases I, II, III, V, VI, VII, VIII or X, or to the set $R^*$ of Case XIII. Consequently every cycle-separating 5-edge-cut of such a minimum counterexample is of Case IV, IX, XI or XII; one side is a 5-cycle and, by the computation of Brinkmann, Goedgebeur, Hägglund and Markström, the other side has at least 33 vertices. The method records, for a Berge–Fulkerson colouring, the pairing of the dangling edges by the Kempe paths of every colour pair. A Kempe switch preserves the pairing of the switched pair and of all disjoint pairs, which gives a finite transition system on labelled boundary states whose greatest fixed point must contain a state of every admissible type. Cases III, VI and XIII are excluded by short hand arguments; for the other six cases the fixed point, computed by a standard-library program and confirmed across all 15 rows of Table 1 by a second independent implementation, has an empty fibre. For Cases IV, IX, XI and XII all fibres survive, so these cases are not decided by route coherence.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Supplement soundness_check.py: replaced the tautological `or True` branch-and-bound condition on line 64 with the exact remaining-matching capacity bound `all(load[k] + (rem - 1) >= 2 for k in range(m))`.
- Supplement independent_fixpoint.py, independent_results.json, compare_implementations.py, compare_implementations.log, README.md, and CONTENTS.sha256 (together with Section 5 of paper.md and the metadata abstract): added `L*` of Case XIII (`XIII-L`) to the second independent implementation so that both implementations cross-check all 15 rows of Table 1 (`ALL_MATCH` across all 15 sets), recorded the 13 and 48 weak-closure failure instances for `R*` and `L*` of Case XIII in Section 5, and refreshed CONTENTS.sha256.
- Sections 1, 2, 3, 6 and References of paper.md: added exact primary-source page/theorem/definition/section citations, issue numbers, DOIs, and arXiv ID to [1]–[5], clarified the isolated-edge convention of [3, 4] in Section 2, and wrote out the one-line parity verification (`n = 2m_c + b_c`) in the proof of Proposition 6.1.
title: Route-coherent Kempe closure and cycle-separating 5-cuts in a minimum counterexample to the Berge–Fulkerson conjecture
